items.notes: Macron called 31 Dec 'the absolute limit' for the loan. Politis cites ERT.
items.text: The extraordinary [[p:European Council]] broke up after about 14 hours without agreeing the 2028–34 budget; the planned second day was cancelled. [[p:António Costa]]'s roughly €1.78tn negotiating box is contested between seven 'frugal' states, who boycotted his small-group format, and 17 'Friends of Cohesion'. The budget and the €45bn Ukraine loan move to the 17–18 Dec summit. Costa says 24 states back the loan; Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia stay out and Bulgaria joins only the civilian strand. Eurozone leaders backed [[p:Pablo Hernández de Cos]] to succeed [[p:Christine Lagarde]] at the ECB.

items.notes: Deaths confirmed; Iranian responsibility is a Kuwaiti claim denied by Tehran.
items.reporter: Yomna Ehab, Elwely Elwelly, Angelo Amante
items.text: Italy's foreign minister said two [[p:Rheinmetall]] Italia technicians were killed when drones hit an air-defence surveillance station in Kuwait; a Pakistani worker and a Kuwaiti officer were wounded. Kuwait's defence ministry blamed Iran and said the deaths came from debris during interceptions. Iran's military denied any offensive operation and called the accusation cover for a 'false flag'. The GCC condemned the attack and [[p:Ursula von der Leyen]] called for more pressure on Iran.

items.notes: UTJ draft-law principles reported by Israeli media via Times of Israel live blog.
items.text: [[p:Gadi Eisenkot]]'s Yashar and [[p:Yair Golan]]'s Democrats agreed to sign a coalition deal after a two-day freeze over ministries, Eisenkot's second partner after [[p:Yisrael Beiteinu]] on 24 Nov. The three parties hold 36 seats, well short of 61; [[p:Naftali Bennett]]'s 12-seat list has not signed. Israeli media report Yashar and UTJ agreed principles of a Haredi draft law. Eisenkot's mandate runs to 6 Dec, extendable by 14 days.

items.notes: Strike warning is a Ukrainian government claim. Meduza confirms the nuclear and restraint remarks, not the deadlock line.
items.text: [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] said intelligence shows Russia is completing preparations for a new mass strike on energy and logistics, and asked for more Patriot interceptors, scarce since the Iran war. US envoy [[p:Jared Kushner]] said talks are at 'a little bit of a deadlock' over territory and that [[p:Vladimir Putin]] had agreed not to use nuclear weapons and shown 'restraint'. [[p:Donald Trump]] urged Putin to pull back military aggression.

items.thread: Russia–Ukraine front line and long-range strikes
items.notes: Figures are Ukrainian official. Borderline Tier 1; context for the strike warning.
items.text: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 155 drones overnight into 27 Nov, with 110 downed or suppressed and hits at 27 locations; one person was killed and at least 16 injured in Zaporizhzhia, and energy and rail sites in Vinnytsia and Zhytomyr were hit, cutting power in six regions. Estonia issued an air-threat warning for six counties and NATO jets were scrambled; no airspace violation was confirmed.

items.notes: Jazan death per Saudi government; 50-target figure is a coalition claim; Ras Tanura claim is Houthi.
items.text: Saudi state media said a [[p:Houthis|Houthi]] strike on the Jazan refinery killed a Nepalese worker and briefly halted some operations. Coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki said the coalition then destroyed 50 military targets in Sanaa, Hodeidah and Saada, including the launcher used against Jazan. The Houthis claimed attacks on Jeddah and Jazan ports and Ras Tanura; the coalition reported interceptions and did not confirm a Ras Tanura hit.

items.notes: KCNA account plus AP reporting; no independent second outlet found.
items.text: State media said [[p:Kim Jong Un]] inspected two nuclear-materials factories, one new and one expanding, plus a nuclear-powered equipment base and a research institute, calling the arsenal irreversible and battlefield low-yield weapons urgent; he named South Korea the 'most dangerous enemy state'. Seoul's defence ministry said it takes the remarks seriously; [[p:Rafael Grossi]] called the Yongbyon enrichment expansion a cause for serious concern.

items.notes: Single intelligence source (HUR); treat with caution.
items.text: Ukraine's military intelligence claims North Korea has temporarily suspended military aid to Russia after Moscow offered in October to mediate between the two Koreas, including halting KN-23 missile and shell deliveries and delaying a Russian request to expand the troop contingent. Neither Moscow nor Pyongyang has confirmed it.

items.notes: Xinhua link covers only the defence ministry remarks.
items.text: Japan's coast guard says two [[p:China Coast Guard]] ships entered waters near the Senkakus and tried to approach a Japanese fishing boat, the fifth such approach this year; Beijing said it lodged representations and took 'necessary control measures'. China's defence ministry separately accused Japan of fuelling South China Sea tensions by supplying radars and drones to the Philippines.

items.notes: China and Brazil positions confirmed; EU, Japan, Singapore, Vietnam reactions from a secondary roundup only. Brazil source in Portuguese.
items.reporter: Zhang Chenxu, Zhong Nan, Lia Zhu
items.text: China's commerce ministry called the proposed [[e:Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974|Section 301]] tariffs typical unilateralism and reserved the right to respond; Brazil said it will not yield and did not rule out a WTO case or reciprocal measures. European Parliament trade chair [[p:Bernd Lange]] reportedly called the 20% EU rate absurd; Japan, Singapore and Vietnam also objected.

items.notes: Strike itself confirmed by Kyiv and eastern Libyan authorities; launch point disputed. Opinion: news and analysis
items.text: Ukraine says seven naval drones hit the Russian corvette Merkury at the Benghazi naval base in [[p:Khalifa Haftar]]'s territory; the ship capsized and partly sank. [[p:Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] said a Ka-27 helicopter was destroyed and a cargo ship he said was carrying weapons was hit. Saddam Haftar said two Libyan naval personnel died. The eastern government asked the UN to investigate whether the drones came from western Libya; Tripoli denies any arrangement with Kyiv, Ukraine's SBU says a 'mother ship' launched them, and UNSMIL called for an independent probe.

items.notes: Summons confirmed; posts reported. Local reporting does not bear out a capture of Walikale (see E-261127-27). Translated from French.
items.text: In posts on X, Ugandan army chief [[p:Muhoozi Kainerugaba]] backed the [[p:Joseph Kabila]]-led FRN's push on Walikale, offered support for seizing Isiro, called Rwanda and Uganda 'twin countries' and said he had ordered troops into eastern Congo. Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner summoned Uganda's head of mission and demanded Kampala's official position; Uganda's government had not commented by 26 Nov.

items.notes: Tchadinfos (citing RFI) says postponed sine die with no new date, likely written before the decree. Translated from French.
items.text: Transitional president Gen. Horta N'Tam issued a decree moving presidential and legislative elections from 6 Dec 2026 to 26 Nov 2028, citing missing technical and financial conditions and a new electoral map that cuts parliament from 102 to 65 seats. It came on the first anniversary of the coup; party activity resumed on 24 Nov but rallies remain banned.

items.notes: Conflicting accounts on Biyara; CTP could not verify most claims. Addis Standard would not load. Opinion: analysis (aggregates ACLED, DW Amharic, Addis Standard)
items.text: Conflict trackers report Ethiopian army artillery moving towards Badme and clashes with Tigrayan forces around Biyara on 21–24 Nov; ACLED says the army took Biyara and Adi Asmerom while other trackers say Tigrayan forces repelled it. DW Amharic reported artillery fire around Badme on 22 Nov. Curfews and weapons registration were ordered in northwestern Tigray.

items.notes: Second link probably not independent.
items.text: [[p:Abiy Ahmed]] told parliament that [[e:Battle of Adwa|Adwa]] {{note: Ethiopian victory over Italian forces in March 1896 under Emperor Menelik II, securing Ethiopia's independence.}} 'will be repeated' if Ethiopia is invaded, while saying it has no plans to attack its neighbours. He named no country.

[[p:Abiy Ahmed]] offered on 23 Nov to host talks among Sudan's military, political and civilian parties towards a unity government. Sudan's army-backed government rejected it, saying Ethiopia lacks neutrality, and asked the AU to keep Addis out, citing its claims that Ethiopia backs the [[p:Rapid Support Forces]]. The RSF-aligned Tasis government and the civilian Sumoud alliance welcomed the offer.

items.notes: Tolls conflict; RSF attribution suspected, not confirmed. Maganza capture is an unverified claim. The National piece is partly analysis.
items.text: Drones struck Ed Damazin and Roseires in Blue Nile on 24 Nov; a local civil-society group says 14 were killed, Emergency Lawyers says 19, and the latter says the Roseires Dam and power facilities were targeted. Neither side commented. An RSF-aligned platform claims Tasis forces took the gold-mining town of Maganza south of Ed Damazin.

items.notes: Sudanese military claims.
items.text: An army mobilisation official announced plans to raise 6,000 fighters along the Ethiopian border in Gedaref, accusing Ethiopia of massing troops; an army-aligned analyst alleged Ethiopian training camps and drone facilities for the RSF. No Ethiopian response or independent verification.
US envoy [[p:Massad Boulos]] said foreign-supplied drones are killing civilians almost daily and urged a swift humanitarian truce and an end to arms flows, after the drone strikes on Khartoum.

The Egyptian, Eritrean and Sudanese foreign ministers met at the Aswan Forum and stressed Red Sea security; in Cairo, PM Kamil Idris and President [[p:Abdel Fattah el-Sisi]] agreed to prioritise Sudan's reconstruction and oppose 'parallel entities'.

items.notes: Defector claim relayed via Middle East Monitor.
items.text: More RSF officers defected, including Col. Adam Abu Daqn on 22 Nov. A defector general claims Israeli experts train RSF cyber units in Nyala; there was no RSF response.

items.notes: Conflicting accounts on mediation.
items.text: [[p:Hassan Sheikh Mohamud]] met [[p:Yoweri Museveni]] in Uganda. Somali Guardian reports he accepted Museveni-mediated talks with the opposition in Mogadishu; a Villa Somalia official called that a fabrication, and the joint communiqué covers only security and trade. Museveni accepted an invitation to visit Mogadishu, no date set.

The cabinet amended the election law so ministers need not resign to run for parliament; PM Hamza Abdi Barre said the vote will be held before May 2027 with the government acting as caretaker. The opposition says the system favours the president's JSP.

items.notes: Garowe's editorial line is strongly critical of Villa Somalia. Expulsion not independently confirmed in this run.
items.text: The cabinet ordered the UAE ambassador out within 72 hours on 19 Nov, and the UAE called the move hostile. On 24 Nov the speaker of parliament alleged, without evidence, that Kenya, Ethiopia and Uganda were colluding with [[p:Al-Shabaab (militant group)|al-Shabaab]] against Mogadishu.

items.notes: Anonymous local sources only. Translated from French.
items.text: FRN rebels took Rurambo and Munanira in the Uvira highlands after about a month of fighting with the Congolese army, Wazalendo militias and Burundian troops, opening a route towards Minembwe and Bijombo; civilians are fleeing the Ruzizi plain.

items.notes: Actualite.cd says claims the FRN is near Kyavinyonge are false. Translated from French.
items.text: The FRN took the Lake Edward fishing settlements of Kanjanja and Talihya in Lubero, its fourth fishery after Nyakakoma, Vitshumbi and Kamandi; the army counterattacked on 25 Nov and fighting continued on 26 Nov. The local administrator calls it a ceasefire violation.

items.notes: Government-side account. Translated from French.
items.text: The army says it repelled FRN attacks at Nzanganano and Luola in Walikale; the attackers withdrew to Malemo in Masisi.

items.notes: No timetable for ambassadors. Togolese press (Le Nouveau Reporter) also covered the Oyo four-way summit.
items.text: At a summit in Oyo hosted by [[p:Denis Sassou Nguesso]], with AU mediator [[p:Faure Gnassingbé]] present, [[p:William Ruto]] and [[p:Félix Tshisekedi]] agreed to restore ambassadors and revive their joint commission, ending the rift over the 2023 launch of the AFC rebel alliance in Nairobi.

items.notes: Data to 24 Nov. Fataki incident per RFI via AllAfrica (https://fr.allafrica.com/stories/202611240291.html).
items.text: ECDC counts 12,021 confirmed Ebola cases and 5,904 deaths in the DRC, up 517 and 274 in a week. A response team was trapped for about 48 hours near Fataki by fighting between the army and [[p:Thomas Lubanga Dyilo|Thomas Lubanga]]'s CRP before evacuation on 23 Nov; Ituri launched a $50m World Bank cash-support programme on 26 Nov.

[[p:Salva Kiir Mayardit|Salva Kiir]] closed the inter-party dialogue, whose resolutions back the 11 Feb 2027 elections, reject another transition extension and call for neutral security forces. Exiled groups were excluded, and voter registration is blocked by insecurity in several areas.
At least 23 people were killed in a cattle-camp attack in Tonj East; the commissioner blames SPLA-IO fighters from Unity State, which a faction denies.

[[p:Chadema]] said it will join reconciliation talks only if [[p:Tundu Lissu]] is freed unconditionally and a neutral international mediator is named; President Samia said on 20 Nov a reconciliation commission would be named soon.
Opposition leaders boycotted an electoral commission meeting, demanded a voter-register audit and electronic results transmission, and threatened protests in January if not met by December.

items.notes: Sonko declared the political divorce from Faye final on 14 Nov. Translated from French.
items.text: National Assembly president [[p:Ousmane Sonko]], removed as PM in May, said he would dissolve the Assembly on 2 Dec, the first legal date, if he had the power, insisted on elections in 2027 and accused President [[p:Bassirou Diomaye Faye]] of fearing a vote.

items.thread: Sahel jihadist insurgency and junta rule
items.notes: Cross-check is AFP. Translated from French.
items.text: Armed assailants attacked a National Guard post at Sanam in Tillabéri; the defence ministry gave a provisional toll of 13 soldiers killed and 20 wounded and said several attackers were killed. No group has claimed it.

items.thread: Sahel jihadist insurgency and junta rule
items.notes: Translated from French.
items.text: [[p:Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal-Muslimin|JNIM]] reportedly ordered residents of Tonka in the Timbuktu region to leave by 27 Nov or face a blockade, citing a new army detachment backed by Russia's Africa Corps. No official Malian response.

items.thread: Sahel jihadist insurgency and junta rule
items.notes: Presidency communiqué.
items.text: [[p:Assimi Goïta]] met army chiefs on readiness and called for intensified operations and closer coordination within the joint force of the [[p:Alliance of Sahel States]].

items.thread: Sahel jihadist insurgency and junta rule
items.notes: AFP on 17 Nov counted 68,381 Burkinabè; Mali counts 79,044 returned. Translated from French. Opinion: partly analysis
items.text: Burkina Faso says it has finished repatriating over 76,000 nationals expelled in Guinea's crackdown on illegal gold mining. Sahel-alliance ministers had called the expulsions massive and uncoordinated, but Mali's PM said Guinea's sovereign decision should not be challenged, a visible split in the alliance.

items.notes: A Sahrawi activist disputes that weapons were surrendered. Both outlets are Moroccan.
items.text: Mauritanian agency Al-Akhbar reports the army detained 14–20 [[p:Polisario Front|Polisario]] fighters who crossed several kilometres into Mauritania and handed over vehicles and weapons; Nouakchott has made no official statement. Mauritania also ordered gold miners out of a 10 km strip along its northern border.

items.notes: Translated from French.
items.text: Exiled opposition figure [[p:Issa Tchiroma Bakary|Issa Tchiroma]], who still claims victory in the 2025 presidential vote, called on the opposition to boycott the 7 Feb 2027 legislative and municipal elections; his party is suspended until 27 Jan. No other party had joined by 25 Nov.

At least 16 people, including women and children, were killed in a night attack on Tafi Gana in Bassa, Plateau State; a local Irigwe association says witnesses saw Fulani among the attackers, which is not independently confirmed.

items.notes: Joburg reconvening per EWN: https://www.ewn.co.za/2026/11/27/joburg-city-council-reconvening-to-elect-new-mayor
items.text: [[p:ActionSA]]'s Nasiphi Moya was re-elected mayor of Tshwane 115–87 over the [[p:Democratic Alliance (South Africa)|DA]]'s Cilliers Brink, with an [[p:Economic Freedom Fighters|EFF]] deputy and an ANC speaker. Johannesburg and Ekurhuleni were due to vote on 27 Nov, with [[p:Herman Mashaba]] the bloc's Joburg candidate; MK reportedly pulled out over Tshwane.

Cabinet approved a bill aligning about a dozen laws with Constitutional Amendment No. 3, which extends terms to seven years and moves elections to 2030; the Constitutional Court reserved judgment on challenges to the amendment on 18 Nov.
Campaigning for the 28 Nov local elections closed; the electoral authority describes the climate as serene.
[[p:Mamady Doumbouya]] ordered ministries to prepare indirect regional elections on 29 Nov and senatorial elections on 20 Dec.
Opposition figure Chaima Issa, sentenced to 20 years in the 'state conspiracy' case, was on day 10 of a hunger strike; a rights group launched a campaign for women detained for their opinions.
IOM says at least 620 people, 456 of them children, fled an armed incursion at Linde in Quissanga district, Cabo Delgado, on 11 Nov.
